chunks: Ali ibn Isa al-Qummi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to me. He said: Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to me from his father, from Khalaf ibn Hammad al-Asadi, from Abu al-Hasan al-Abdi, from Sulayman ibn Mihran, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:
O Ali! You are my brother, my inheritor, my deputy, and my vicegerent among my family and my Nation, in my lifetime and after my death. One who loves you loves me, and one who hates you hates me.

O Ali! You and I are the two fathers of this Nation. O Ali! I, you, and the Imams from your descendants are masters in this life and kings in the Hereafter. Whoever recognizes us has recognized Allah, and whoever denies us has denied Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

key_terms.خَلِيفَة: Khalifa - Vicegerent: the appointed representative and successor in leadership of the Muslim community
key_terms.سَادَة: Sada - Masters/Leaders: those of the highest rank and authority, denoting spiritual and temporal leadership in this world
key_terms.مُلُوك: Muluk - Kings: sovereigns in the Hereafter, indicating supreme spiritual authority and elevated station in the afterlife
key_terms.وَارِث: Warith - Inheritor: one who receives the Prophet's spiritual and authoritative legacy, implying succession in both knowledge and leadership
key_terms.وَصِيّ: Wasi - Deputy/Executor: the designated successor entrusted with carrying out the Prophet's mission and safeguarding his teachings after his passing

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about Ali being his brother and successor?
ai.summary: In this prophetic tradition from al-Amali of Sheikh al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (s) addresses Imam Ali (as) in the presence of the community, declaring him his brother, inheritor, deputy, and vicegerent among both his family and the broader Muslim nation, in his lifetime and after his death. The Prophet further declares that love for Ali equates to love for the Prophet, and hatred for Ali equates to hatred for the Prophet. He then elevates their station by calling himself and Ali the two fathers of the nation, and asserts that he, Ali, and the Imams from Ali's descendants are masters in this world and kings in the Hereafter. The hadith concludes with the profound theological statement that recognizing them is equivalent to recognizing Allah, and denying them is equivalent to denying Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

en.bilal-muhammad: `Ali b. `Isa al-Qummi (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. Muhammad Majiluwayh narrated to me. He said: Ahmad b. Abi `Abdillah al-Barqi narrated to me from his father from Khalaf b. Hammad al-Asadi from Abi’l Hasan al-`Abdi from Sulayman b. Mehran from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers from `Ali (as). He said: The Messenger of Allah (s) said:

O `Ali! You are my brother, my inheritor, my deputy, and my vicegerent (khalifa) among my family and my Nation, in my lifetime and after my death. Love for you is love for me, and hatred for you is hatred for me.

O `Ali! You and I are the two fathers of this Nation. O `Ali! I, yourself, and the Imams from your descendants are masters in this life and kings in the Hereafter. He who recognizes us has recognized Allah, and he who denies us has denied Allah.
